utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Could the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-95-14-R77.2-I, the Prosecutor against Ivica Marijacic and Markica Rebic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: May I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, David Akerson, on behalf of the OTP, with Jason Dominguez on my right and case manager, Sebastian van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Akerson. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a member of the Croatian bar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you state your name, please, again for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Marin Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the Defence for Mr. Marijacic -- I'm sorry, Ivica Marijacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Kresimir Krsnik and I am Defence counsel for Mr. Markica Rebic. I'm a member of the Croatian bar, and I'm here in my capacity as lead counsel. Together with me is Mr. Veljko Miljevic, also a member of the Croatian bar and both of us are lawyers in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krsnik. Mr. Marijacic and Mr. Rebic, please correct me if I'm wrong in pronunciation. Can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED MARIJACIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could please stand and state your full name, please. Who would go first? Mr. Marijacic first. THE ACCUSED MARIJACIC: [Interpretation] My name is Ivica Marijacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you please state the date and place of your birth. THE ACCUSED MARIJACIC: [Interpretation] I was born on the 25th of January, 1958, in Nadin, that is the place, near Benkovac, a town in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rebic. THE ACCUSED REBIC: [Interpretation] My name is Markica Rebic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And would you state the date and place of your birth as well. THE ACCUSED REBIC: [Interpretation] I was born on the 11th of November, 1951, in a place called Imotski in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. This hearing is the initial appearance of Mr. Ivica Marijacic and Mr. Markica Rebic. This hearing is to be conducted in accordance with Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. As stipulated in the order of 27th of May, 2005, a Status Conference will follow the initial appearance. The indictment against the accused was confirmed by a Judge of the Tribunal on 26th of April, 2005. On 5th of May, 2005, the President assigned this case to Trial Chamber III and I was appointed by the Chamber as the Presiding Judge as well as Pre-Trial Judge to preside over this case. The first matter will be the indictment. Mr. Ivanovic and Krsnik, I take it that your clients have received a copy of the indictment in a language that they understand and that you have had the opportunity of going through it with them. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're certainly right. And the indictment need not be read out today as we are fully apprised of its contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The same is the case with Mr. Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then the next step is then entry of a plea to the charge of the indictment. The accused may enter a plea within 30 days of the initial appearance but he may enter a plea at the time of initial appearance, if he so wishes. So Mr. Ivanovic, and Mr. Krsnik, does your client wish to enter a plea today or do it later?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client wishes to enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same with my client, Your Honour. Since we're here, we see no reason to postpone the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. If Mr. Marijacic and Rebic could rise. Please plead to the count of the indictment which I will read out to you and please confine your answer to either guilty or not guilty. Count 1 or the only count of the indictment charges you with contempt of the Tribunal punishable pursuant to Rule 77(A)(ii) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, which provides that the Tribunal in the exercise of its inherent power may hold in contempt those who knowingly and wilfully interfere with its administration of justice, including any person who discloses information relating to those proceedings in knowing violation of an order of a Chamber. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? Mr. Marijacic. THE ACCUSED MARIJACIC: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Rebic. THE ACCUSED REBIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. I would like to ask the registrar to note that both of the accused have pleaded not guilty to the indictment. I am now going to deal, as mentioned at the outset, with some of the issues that are normally on the agenda of a Status Conference in this Tribunal. The purpose of a Status Conference is to organise exchanges between the parties, so as to ensure an expeditious preparation for the trial and also to give an opportunity to the accused in particular to raise any issues in relation to their case, including mental or physical conditions. The first matter would be the disclosure. I must now remind the Prosecution that pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), "the Prosecutor shall make available to the Defence in a language the accused understands within 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused, copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment as well as any prior statements obtained by the Prosecutor from the accused." However, may I take it that this disclosure could be completed today?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this disclosure will be available first thing tomorrow morning, 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now turn to the Defence, that the Defence will have a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motions that it may care to do once it has received all of the supporting material in accordance with Rule 66 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. It may be a bit too early to ask this, but do you have any observation in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Ivica Marijacic, the first accused, immediately after this Status Conference will file a motion to reject the indictment, considering that it is not in conformity with the Rules, but we consider that the questions set out in our motion have to be dealt with first. So we are quite ready to communicate with the parties and proceed as directed by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Markica Rebic will do the same. Immediately after this Status Conference it will file a motion with the same motives explained by Mr. Ivanovic a moment ago. And secondly, I think that with our learned colleagues of the Prosecution, we will have to sit down to a negotiating table and see how we will proceed with the case and anything that is not clear will be clarified during that meeting I hope. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to turn to the Prosecutor again. I would like to ask the situation in relation to other disclosure. Is there any -- anything in particular in relation to Rule 66 (A)(ii) and 68 disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I don't think there are going to be significant amounts of disclosure. I think that will be straightforward and we'll be able to deal with it very promptly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you think about my setting a timetable for that disclosure? How long would you need for that disclosure to be completed?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: If I could just have one moment to confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that we will be able to Pristina all disclosure within 30 days, but there is a caveat, there is an ongoing investigation. And that additional investigation may yield additional disclosure. These are incidents -- earlier incidents that may result in additional charges. We're not -- we haven't concluded that investigation yet, so we aren't certain that that will happen. But as it stands right now with the current indictments, 30 days will be sufficient to complete all disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Of course it will be dependant upon the result of the motion the Defence is going to file, but apart from that how many witnesses do you have in mind to call at the hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Very few, and I think we are going to confer with Defence counsel after this hearing. This may be one of the rare cases where there's very little factual dispute, that it is almost an appellate argument where it is just legal issues. I think there may be one or two witnesses that may need to be called, but I can't answer that with complete certainty until I meet with Defence counsel and get their sense of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said one or two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Well, if all goes as planned, I think in the worst-case scenario, you're probably looking at five witnesses. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have statements of those witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: All of that material will be available, with the exception of a possible expert witness that we're looking to secure at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So there would be no problem to disclose all those materials you have got at this moment to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning -- maybe by the end of today even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I wish to say is this: The Defence is in no hurry with respect to the materials and with respect to the motion, and I agree with my learned colleague, we're dealing with legal issues. And I think that according to our law, and this is something that common law knows, too, there is a prejudicial question. So let's settle the legal issues first, and we'll see whether there's a trial at all. And in conformity with that, all I wish to say is what the position of the Defence is, and it is this: We can wait with the disclosure of the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I see your point. Then we'll wait for the Defence motion and see what we can do. Is there any other matters the party wish to raise at this moment? Yes, Mr. Akerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I just have one comment and one matter. From our perspective, Your Honour, since it is a contempt case, it does seem important that the case be tried in as close proximity to the time of the offence, rather than let it drag out, so we are interested in having a very quick trial, as quickly as it could be arranged. Secondly, we were informed by a colleague yesterday that on the Hrvatski List web site, the material that is the subject of the contempt allegation is still on their web site. I've provided a copy of -- a print-out of the web site to Defence counsel and they have raised the question of whether or not it is their web site. So there is some uncertainty, but I would ask Your Honour to advise the accused that they are still subject to a cease and desist order that was issued by the Court on December 2nd, and if the material that is -- was the subject of the cease and desist order is on their web site, they are still -- that would be considered a contempt allegation. So we would ask this Court to advise them to remove all material that was named in the cease and desist order, if it is in fact on their web site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I state here that Hrvatski List does not have its web site and everybody can publish any material over the Internet. And what the Prosecution sent in today quite simply goes against the grain of all the rules of proceedings. So at a Status Conference they are sending in a document which somebody - who knows who - put on the Internet. That is not the subject of this case. The Hrvatski List paper does not have its Internet site and it does not stand behind the fact that these materials were made public on the Internet. And at the same time with your permission, and the Court's indulgence, could I caution the Prosecutor. There was some errors of fact. The Hrvatski List is not published in Belgrade, nor was it -- nor did it -- in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Zagreb, nor did it publish any material related to the case and the trial. So I should like to ask that the indictment be corrected. Those are errors of fact which the Prosecutor has made in this particular case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivanovic. I heard that both parties are minded to meet together, sit together, and discuss the case. So please take -- I would very much encourage the parties to discuss this matter as well and if Prosecution is not satisfied, it can file a motion in relation to this. We will see what will come at a later stage. Is there any other matters from the Defence? Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one matter, Your Honour, that I'd like to raise perhaps. The Croatian government is very upset because of these proceedings because we are dealing with the freedom of the press and other matters related to that. And when the Prosecutor today said that there was an additional investigation that was ongoing, I should like to ask him whether those -- the investigations are secret or public because it will give rise to greater unrest among the public. If it is not secret, then we'd like to know whether those investigations relate to this case, if that is at all possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder if Mr. Akerson could respond to this observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not at liberty to discuss the ongoing investigation at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. In terms of scheduling of a trial, it may depend upon the motion the Defence is going to file, but if a trial is to take place at all, when do you think we can have a trial? From the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the Defence Mr. Marijacic is concerned, we are ready at all times. Any time is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about Mr. Rebic's case?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course the Defence is trial-ready, but we expect the indictment to be rejected and we are really convinced that there will be no trial. It won't come to trial. But if it comes to trial, of course the disclosure of material and for that issue the Defence has to prepare itself. As for Markica Rebic, we have to approach the matter seriously, if it does come to trial ultimately at all, because we are not only dealing with Mr. Rebic but we are dealing with a dangerous precedent as far as the freedom of the media and press are concerned, not in only in Croatia but all over the world, in the whole globe. And we will certainly have to prepare for that and I don't think that could be before the end of the year, as far as Mr. Markica Rebic's defence is concerned. Because when you read our motion and add our motion where we claim that the Prosecution have overstepped its authorisations quite a bit, and as it is the sole Prosecution which is the subject of no control, then of course we had to set out all our views and positions in the motion. We'll see the outcome of that in due course, and we'll be able to answer when we shall be trial-ready. But as I said, by the end of the year I hope, roughly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, the end of this year?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll see. And I wonder if you'll be in the position to answer the question that if we come to the trial ever, how many witnesses you are going to call at the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is difficult at this point in time. You understand, it's difficult for me to answer your question before we can see what witnesses the Prosecution is going to provide. Only after that will we be able to decide on strategy and procedure because it will depend on the Prosecution witnesses. We will have to respond adequately with our own witnesses. So it's difficult for me to say at this point in time, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the Defence of Mr. Marijacic is concerned, we cannot give you an answer today until the prejudicial questions and issues are solved and until we can see the Prosecution's stand vis-a-vis the whole proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understand the point. Is there any matter the Defence wishes to raise today? Mr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Mr. Marijacic would like to present the following, the basic grounds of this proceedings and its views. The Prosecution, with the indictment, did not send out any Court order which would be addressed to Mr. Marijacic and which Mr. Marijacic could violate then. Mr. Marijacic was not able to violate any Court order because he was not issued with any Court order and no Court order referred urbi et orbi but related to the person to whom it is issued, and therefore this indictment is not conducive to discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Akerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I would just like to say, Your Honour, I think those are issues for trial and not for this hearing and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Thank you. Unless there's further issues to be raised, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: adjourned at 10.29 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
